items.h: Ja'Marr Chase (ankle) off injury report for Week 8
items.s: Ja'Marr Chase (ankle) is off of the injury report for Week 8 for the Cincinnati Bengals according to Paul Dehner Jr. Chase is good to go after battling ankle issues earlier in the week, boosting a Cincinnati passing attack for Week 8.

items.h: Ja'Marr Chase Due For A Breakout Game Against Tennessee
items.s: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase will face the Tennessee Titans at home in Week 8. The Bengals superstar racked up five catches for 62 yards and a touchdown in last week's win over the Baltimore Ravens. Chase has not reached 100 receiving yards in any game this season and this week is as good a spot as any to change that. The Titans defense is not a unit to avoid this season and Chase is a must-start player every week regardless of the matchup. Chase has not given fantasy managers any of his vintage week-winning performances this year, but they're likely on the way given his immense talent and strong offensive environment. Chase is ranked WR4 in our RotoBaller Week 8 PPR…

items.h: Ja'Marr Chase will play in Week 8 vs. the Titans
items.s: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase (ankle) practiced again on Friday and will play in Week 8 against the visiting Tennessee Titans, as expected, according to Kelsey Conway of The Cincinnati Enquirer. Chase came out of the Week 7 win over the division-rival Baltimore Ravens with some ankle soreness and was rested in Wednesday's practice, creating speculation that he might be questionable to play this week. The star wideout returned to practice the next day, though, and should be a full-go on Sunday at home against the one-win Titans, making him a set-and-forget high-end WR1 for fantasy lineups. The 26-year-old has not exactly lived up to expectations so far through the first…

items.h: Ja'Marr Chase Appears on Track to Play Against Titans
items.s: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase (ankle) was on the practice field Friday, preparing to catch passes from quarterback Joe Burrow, according to Kelsey Conway of The Cincinnati Enquirer. Chase was seen jumping up and down during warmups, another encouraging sign for his availability ahead of Sunday's Week 8 matchup against the Tennessee Titans. The 26-year-old missed Wednesday's practice with an ankle injury and rest designation before returning as a full participant Thursday. Chase caught five of seven targets for 62 yards and a touchdown in last week's victory over the Baltimore Ravens, giving him 32 receptions for 351 yards and five touchdowns through six games. RotoBaller's…

items.h: No limitations Thursday
items.s: Chase (ankle) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Mike Petraglia of CLNSCincy.com reports. After sitting out Wednesday's session, Chase assuaged any concerns regarding his availability for Sunday's game against the Titans by practicing without limitations Thursday. The star wide receiver will look to pick up the pace following what has been a slow start by his lofty standards. Chase is averaging a career-low 58.5 receiving yards per game after notching at least 76 yards per game in each of the previous five regular seasons.

items.h: Ja'Marr Chase a Full Practice Participant on Thursday
items.s: Cincinnati Bengals star wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase (ankle) was listed as a full participant in practice on Thursday after he was held out on Wednesday, mainly for rest purposes, according to Adam Schefter of ESPN. There were concerns about Chase's Week 8 status when he did not see the field at all on Wednesday, but his ankle injury is not a major concern, and he is fully expected to play this Sunday at home against the Tennessee Titans. The 26-year-old former fifth overall pick in the 2021 NFL draft out of LSU has not lived up to being the first receiver off the board in most fantasy drafts this year, with 32 receptions for 351 yards in six games played, but he has made up for some of it…

items.h: In uniform Thursday
items.s: Chase (ankle) is in uniform for Thursday's practice, Charlie Goldsmith of Fox 19 Now Cincinnati reports. Chase has resumed practicing after sitting out Wednesday's session due to a listed combination of rest/ankle. Thursday's return to action supports an earlier report from Ian Rapoport of NFL Network that Chase isn't dealing with a significant ankle issue, though it remains to be seen whether the wideout is able to practice without limitations. The 4-2 Bengals will face the 1-6 Titans on Sunday.

items.h: Ja'Marr Chase (ankle) in uniform for practice Thursday
items.s: Ja'Marr Chase was seen in uniform for practice on Thursday. Chase missed practice to begin the week on Wednesday. He'll need to continue to be monitored on the injury report.

items.h: Ja'Marr Chase not believed to be dealing with serious ankle injury
items.s: Ja'Marr Chase's ankle injury "is not considered a major deal." Chase missed practice on Wednesday with the ankle injury. He'll need to continue to be monitored in practice on Thursday and Friday.

items.h: Ja'Marr Chase in Uniform for Thursday's Practice
items.s: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase (ankle) is in uniform for Thursday's practice, according to Charlie Goldsmith of FOX 19. Chase did not practice on Wednesday, but it was primarily for rest purposes, and the NFL Network's Ian Rapoport said that Chase's ankle injury is nothing major and that he is expected to play without restrictions in Sunday's Week 8 contest against the Tennessee Titans. The 26-year-old Pro Bowler should return to full practice by Friday and eventually be cleared from the final Week 8 injury report, so fantasy managers should have nothing to worry about as far as Chase's health status this week. The former fifth overall pick from LSU has yet to record a…

items.h: Expected to play against Titans
items.s: Chase (ankle) isn't believed to be dealing with a serious injury, and he's expected to suit up Sunday against the Titans, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Chase was listed as a non-participant at Wednesday's practice due to an ankle injury, but the injury isn't expected to keep him from taking the field Sunday. His participation in practice will still bear monitoring as the week unfolds. Chase has two chances left to resume practicing without limitations, which would put him in position to avoid a Week 8 injury designation.

items.h: Ja'Marr Chase Expected to Play in Week 8
items.s: Cincinnati Bengals star wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase (ankle) was rested in Wednesday's practice with an ankle injury, but it is not considered to be a major deal, and Chase is expected to be out there for the team's Week 8 game this Sunday against the visiting Tennessee Titans, according to Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network. The Bengals apparently held Chase out of the first practice of the week more for rest purposes, so he should be back at practice on Thursday and Friday and be available for fantasy managers this weekend as a must-start WR1 in a smash spot against the one-win Titans. The 26-year-old five-time Pro Bowler and two-time first-team All-Pro has caught 32 of his 45 targets for…

items.h: Ja'Marr Chase (ankle/rest) misses practice Wednesday
items.s: Ja'Marr Chase did not practice on Wednesday. Chase was listed on the injury report with an ankle issue as well as it being a rest day. He'll need to be monitored in practice on Thursday.

items.h: Receives maintenance for ankle Wednesday
items.s: Chase was listed as a non-participant in Wednesday's practice due to an ankle injury and rest, Ben Baby of ESPN.com reports. Though Chase was absent to kick off Week 8 prep, Jay Morrison of SI.com notes that the star wideout was presumably held out for maintenance-related reasons rather than out of concern about his ankle. As long as Chase is able to get back on the field in some capacity Thursday or Friday, he should be ready to go for Sunday's game against the Titans.

items.h: Ja'Marr Chase not seen at practice Wednesday
items.s: Ja'Marr Chase was not seen at practice on Wednesday. It is unclear what the reason is for the absence of Chase to begin the week. He'll need to be monitored on the official injury report.

items.h: Absent from Wednesday stretch
items.s: Chase wasn't spotted during the stretch portion of Wednesday's practice, Mike Petraglia of CLNSCincy.com reports. Chase previously dealt with a concussion this season, but he was able to play a full allotment of snaps on either side of the Bengals' Week 6 bye, totaling an 11-139-2 line on 17 targets in those contests. It's unclear if he's tending to a health concern to begin Week 8 prep, or if he's merely getting a veteran rest day.

items.h: Chase brought in five of seven targets for 62 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals' 35-13 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
items.s: Chase played a clear second fiddle to Tee Higgins, who had a team-high 148 receiving yards, as the former finished second to his teammate in receptions and receiving yards while tying him for the team lead in targets. Chase also recorded a touchdown grab for the second straight game, bringing in a two-yard scoring strike from Joe Burrow at the halfway point of the fourth quarter. Chase is still in search of his first 100-yard game of the season, and he'll look to break the ice on that front in a Week 8 home matchup against a vulnerable Titans secondary next Sunday.

items.h: Chase brought in six of 10 targets for 77 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals' 31-24 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
items.s: Chase was ultimately able to clear concussion protocol just before Sunday's game after exiting the Week 4 loss to the Jaguars with the head injury, and he finished as the Bengals' leader in all of receptions, receiving yards and targets against Miami. The star receiver capped off his productive day with a stellar one-handed, contested 45-yard touchdown grab in the waning moments of the third quarter. Chase is up to a 27-289-4 receiving line on the season despite having missed more than a half against Jacksonville, and he'll next tangle with the division-rival Ravens' veteran secondary in a…

items.h: Chase (concussion) is active for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
items.s: Forced out early in last Sunday's loss to the Jaguars after sustaining a concussion, Chase was a spectator for the Bengals' first Week 5 practice Wednesday before upgrading to limited activity Thursday and full participation Friday. He carried a questionable tag into Sunday's contest, but after passing the final stage of the five-step concussion protocol by gaining clearance from an independent neurologist, Chase has been deemed ready to play. Tee Higgins (groin/neck) is also suiting up after being listed as questionable, so quarterback Joe Burrow will have his top two targets available for…

items.h: Chase (concussion) is slated to play Sunday at Miami, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
items.s: The same goes for fellow WR Tee Higgins (groin/neck) after both endured practice restrictions during Week 5 prep but capped it with full sessions Friday. Chase himself made quick work of the protocol for head injuries after he was ripped to the ground via his facemask last Sunday against the Jaguars. On the season, he boasts a 21-212-3 line on 28 targets in parts of four contests.

items.h: Chase remains in concussion protocol and will be listed as questionable for Sunday's game at Miami, Charlie Goldsmith of Fox 19 Now Cincinnati reports.
items.s: Chase practiced fully Friday but will still need clearance from an independent neurologist to be able to play Sunday. Fellow Bengals wideout Tee Higgins (adductor) didn't practice before Friday, when he was full, and he could be in more danger of missing Week 5.

items.h: Chase (concussion) is in uniform for Friday's practice, Charlie Goldsmith of Fox 19 Now Cincinnati reports.
items.s: Chase remains in the league's concussion protocol, and while it's a good sign he's on the field for Friday's practice, it doesn't yet mean he's cleared all the necessary steps to play Sunday against the Dolphins. The Bengals will post official injury designations later Friday, and fantasy managers will then have a better idea of the star wideout's availability for Week 5.

items.h: Chase (concussion) was officially listed as a limited participant at Thursday's practice, Ben Baby of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Chase took a step in the right direction Thursday after being unable to practice Wednesday. In order to have a chance to clear the league's five-step concussion protocol in time to suit up Sunday against the Dolphins, Chase would need to practice without limitations Friday. He was diagnosed with a concussion after exiting this past Sunday's loss to the Jaguars in the first half.

items.h: Chase (concussion) was present for the media-access portion of Thursday's practice, Ben Baby of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: In the wake of his rough exit from this past Sunday's game against the Jaguars, Chase has been embedded in the concussion protocol and sat out Wednesday's session, but his return one day later indicates he's making some progress through it. Thursday's injury report will reveal his activity level, as well as that of fellow WR Tee Higgins (groin/neck).

items.h: Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said that Chase remains in concussion protocol and won't practice Wednesday, Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic reports.
items.s: Chase sustained a concussion in the first half of last Sunday's loss to the Jaguars and isn't certain to clear the five-step protocol in time for the Bengals' Week 5 game against the Dolphins. Tee Higgins (adductor) is expected to be a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, so if one or both of Cincinnati's top two wideouts are sidelined, receiver Dohnte Meyers and tight end Mike Gesicki could be in store for notable spikes in their target shares.

items.h: Knockout league pickups: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Ja'Marr Chase among big names available in Week 5
items.s: Tristan H. Cockcroft lists the most common players on eliminated teams and finds how much FAB to spend this week.

items.h: Week 4 winners and losers: Tetairoa McMillan, CeeDee Lamb dominate; Jaxon Smith-Njigba struggles
items.s: CeeDee Lamb and Kyren Williams came up big in Week 4, while Jaxon Smith-Njigba and D'Andre Swift had disappointing days.

items.h: Chase (concussion) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
items.s: Chase was taken out of the game to be checked for a possible concussion after his facemask was pulled at the end of a four-yard catch in the second quarter. With the superstar wide receiver done for the day, Tee Higgins will be Joe Burrow's top target in the passing game, with Dohnte Meyers, Mitchell Tinsley, running back Chase Brown and tight end Mike Gesicki all in line for bigger roles for the rest of the game. Chase will need to clear the league's five-step concussion protocol in order to be available for Week 5 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Oct. 11.

items.h: Chase is under evaluation for a possible concussion during Sunday's game versus the Jaguars.
items.s: Chase was ripped down by his facemask on a four-yard catch by a Jacksonville defender in the second quarter and remained on the turf before hitting the sidelines and eventually going to the locker room. If he ends up entering the protocol for head injuries, he'll be out for the rest of Week 4, and Tee Higgins, Dohnte Meyers and Mitchell Tinsley will be tasked with WR duties for the rest of Sunday.

items.h: Chase brought in nine of 12 targets for 98 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals' 30-27 loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
items.s: Chase paced the Bengals in receptions, receiving yards and targets, taking his customary position at the top of the team's pass-catching corps. The All-Pro wideout recorded his touchdown on a three-yard grab with just under six minutes remaining in the first quarter to answer a Steelers opening-drive score, marking his third trip to the end zone already this season. Chase will aim to stay just as productive when the Jaguars pay a visit for a Week 4 showdown next Sunday.

items.h: Week 2 winners and losers: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, CeeDee Lamb shine; Bijan Robinson struggles
items.s: Jaxon Smith-Njigba and CeeDee Lamb came up big in Week 2, while Bijan Robinson and Justin Jefferson had very quiet days.

items.h: Chase brought in seven of nine targets for 75 yards and two touchdowns in the Bengals' 20-6 win over the Texans on Sunday.
items.s: Chase recorded what already profiles as a Catch of the Year candidate on the first of his two touchdowns, one that saw him exhibit elite body control while making a narrowly inbounds, spinning grab from 32 yards out late in the second quarter. He went on to add an 18-yard TD reception in the latter portion of the third quarter as well, and he finished with the team lead in receptions while checking in as the runner-up to Tee Higgins in both receiving yards and targets. The rewarding fantasy day atoned for a quiet two-reception and scoreless Week 1 for the perennial Pro Bowler, who'll next…

items.h: Unwavering confidence in Loveland, concern for Pitts and more to ponder going into Week 2
items.s: Adam Rank catches you up on the vital information and insight needed to make tough lineup decisions in Week 2.

items.h: Chase said Thursday that his knee feels great, Kelsey Conway of the Cincinnati Enquirer reports.
items.s: Chase sustained a knee injury in practice Aug. 25 but hasn't seemed bothered by it recently, as he suited up for the Week 1 win over the Buccaneers and has been practicing without limitations ahead of Sunday's road matchup with Houston. The star wide receiver had a disappointing 12 receiving yards against the Buccaneers, but starting slow has become the norm for Chase, who had 39, 62 and 26 receiving yards in the preceding three season openers. He bounced back from his 26-yard Week 1 showing in 2025 with 165 yards and a touchdown in Week 2.

items.h: Pickens, Chase highlight Fantasy football Knockout league pickups for Week 2
items.s: Tristan H. Cockcroft lists the most common players on eliminated teams and finds how much FAB to spend this week.

items.h: Week 1 winners and losers: Caleb Williams and Josh Allen dominate; Ja'Marr Chase disappoints
items.s: Caleb Williams, Josh Allen and Trevor Lawrence came up big in Week 1, while Ja'Marr Chase, Drake London and Colston Loveland had very quiet days.

items.h: Chase brought in two of four targets for 12 yards in the Bengals' 33-27 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
items.s: Despite the Bengals shaking off their usual Week 1 offensive doldrums, it was still a relatively modest day for the air attack. Joe Burrow threw for a respectable 254 yards, but Chase wasn't prioritized anywhere near the norm and actually finished behind all of Mike Gesicki, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown in targets. Chase will continue to be the focal point of opposing defenses every week, but he should be in line for more opportunity in a Week 2 road matchup against a Texans defense that was surprisingly gashed by the Bills on Sunday.

items.h: Chase (knee) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against Tampa Bay.
items.s: Chase was a full practice participant Wednesday and Thursday before resting Friday, with the Bengals citing 'rest' rather than his knee as the reason for Friday's absence. He suffered a minor knee hyperextension Aug. 25 and returned to practice within two weeks. Chase should be ready for his usual role this Sunday against the Buccaneers.

items.h: Chase (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Paul Dehner of The Athletic reports.
items.s: It's looking promising for Chase's status going into the season-opener after his full practice Wednesday. He had a knee injury scare in August but has been present for practices since the beginning of the week. At this stage, Chase should be good to go for the season-opener against the Buccaneers.

items.h: Coach Zac Taylor said Wednesday he "feels good" about Chase (knee) playing Sunday against the Bucs, Jay Morrison of SI.com reports.
items.s: Chase limped off the field late last month with a left knee injury, but there's been nothing to suggest he's in any real danger of missing the season opener versus Tampa Bay. In a potential shootout with the Bucs, Chase is looking like the premier wide receiver play on the board for Week 1 in fantasy.

items.h: Chase (knee) is in uniform for Monday's practice, Charlie Goldsmith of Charlie's Chalkboard reports.
items.s: Chase limped off the practice field on Aug. 25 and was diagnosed with a hyperextended left knee. Prior to Monday, he hasn't logged any visible on-field work in the meantime, so his ability to suit up indicates he'll at least be able to get involved in individual drills. The Bengals will be posting their first Week 1 injury report Wednesday, at which point his activity level will became known as the team prepares for Sunday's game against the Bengals.

items.h: Adam Schefter's fantasy football cheat sheet: Value picks and sleepers to target
items.s: The annual favorite is back, featuring Adam's favorite picks at each level of the draft, including sleepers.

items.h: Chase (knee) was present but not suited up at Wednesday's practice, Gabi Sorrentino of Fox 19 Cincinnati reports.
items.s: Coach Zac Taylor told Ben Baby of ESPN.com on Tuesday that Chase would be limited this week, but he "feels good about" the wide receiver after he hyperextended his left knee while attempting to gather in a deep ball at practice early last week. Just one day later, though, Chase didn't mix into any drills, and fellow WR Tee Higgins joined him on the sideline due to his own heel injury. The statuses of the Bengals' top options at the position thus are up in the air as Week 1 approaches.

items.h: Coach Zac Taylor said Tuesday that Chase (knee) will be a limited participant in practice this week, and he "feels good about" where the wide receiver stands, Ben Baby of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Chase injured his left knee last Tuesday when he attempted to catch a deep ball and had an awkward landing. He exhibited a visible limp in the aftermath, but he later told Kelsey Conway of The Cincinnati Enquirer that it was a "little hyperextension," and he could have resumed practicing. Chase will attempt to put the issue behind him ahead of a Week 1 matchup with the Buccaneers on Sunday, Sept. 13.

items.h: Chase (knee) is not participating in Wednesday's practice, Ben Baby of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Chase downplayed the injury that forced him from Tuesday's session, but he will get at least one day to rest and recover. The report notes that Chase "was not sporting any protective equipment," which backs up his stance that he is dealing only with a minor setback.

items.h: Chase (knee) said Tuesday that he could play in a game Wednesday after exiting Tuesday's practice early, Kelsey Conway of the Cincinnati Enquirer reports.
items.s: Chase has spent Tuesday afternoon downplaying his hyperextended knee, so this seems like it will be a non-issue moving forward after he came down awkwardly at the end of practice. The star wide receiver is a cinch top-five fantasy pick as Joe Burrow's alpha wideout.

items.h: Chase downplayed his knee injury Tuesday, saying it was a "little hyperextension," and he could've kept practicing, Kelsey Conway of the Cincinnati Enquirer reports.
items.s: Chase came up limping at the tail end of Tuesday's session when he jumped for a deep ball and landed awkwardly. He immediately left the field and was tended to by the training staff before shooing them away and remaining on the sidelines for the remainder of practice. It sounds like Chase will be fine well in time for the Bengals' regular-season opener in a little less than three weeks.

items.h: Chase (knee) limped off the field at Tuesday's practice after landing awkwardly while attempting to reel in a deep ball, Jay Morrison of SI.com reports.
items.s: Chase was favoring his left knee after the play in question, but he was able to walk to the sideline under his own power with trainers, per Charlie Clifford of NBC 5 Cincinnati. Potentially a major development for the Bengals offense, Chase's status should receive some clarity after Tuesday's session.
